title: Variant dedupe and semantic naming rollout for buttons/tables/charts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Scope: Reduce variant bloat and enforce a new semantic naming convention across Buttons, Tables, and Chart components in the Figma library. Goals: (1) Identify and deduplicate semantically identical variants (visual or layout duplicates that differ only by token aliasing or size labels), (2) Standardize auto-layout constraints and content hugging so components behave predictably when nested, (3) Adopt a semantic naming pattern: <component> / <role> / <state> / <size> (e.g., Button / primary / pressed / md), (4) Implement alias components for backward compatibility and prepare a publishing checklist and rollout notes for product teams.

Acceptance criteria: 1) No more than one canonical variant per semantic combination (role+state+size) for each component family. 2) Auto-layout consolidation applied to canonical components with consistent padding tokens and min-width behavior. 3) A migration alias layer exists in the library for at least two weeks (aliases map old names to new canonical components). 4) Documentation and release notes published in Confluence and a short changelog pinned in the Design System Slack channel. 5) QA checklist executed against top 6 product screens that use these components and sign-off from two product designers.

Work breakdown (high level):
- Audit: run a variance matrix for Buttons/Tables/Charts to find duplicates and layout divergences.
- Decisions: pick canonical tokens (token IDs) to use for padding/spacing/typography for canonical variants.
- Implementation: (a) create canonical components, (b) create alias components with a visible migration banner instance, (c) fix auto-layout constraints across canonical components.
- Docs & rollout: update Figma library README, publish Confluence doc with migration steps, announce via Slack, schedule 1:1 walkthroughs with platform PMs.

Risks & trade-offs: Consolidating variants reduces library size and complexity but may require product teams to update overrides where they relied on non-canonical quirks. To reduce friction, we'll keep aliases for two weeks and provide a codemod-style PR template for front-end engineers to update classnames/variants. If a product team objects to a canonical choice, create a short-lived forked variant and escalate to DS guild for final arbitration.
